第 62 章 Onboarding Beyond Codelabs超越 Codelab 的入职

Jean Hsu / 让·徐

— 第 178 页 —

When we think about onboarding process, we often think about codelabs, classes, and tutorials. And let's face it, at most high-growth startups, it can never seem like the right time to spin up a project to build out more onboarding resources. Many years ago, I implemented two subtle but powerful changes to Medium's onboarding process. Surprisingly, neither is engineering specific nor have to do with code walkthroughs or tutorials at all. I share them with you here, along with a third bonus tip for building alignment quickly with a new member of your team.

当我们想到入职流程时，我们经常想到 codelab、课程和教程。面对现实吧，在大多数高增长创业公司，似乎永远不是启动一个项目来建设更多入职资源的合适时机。很多年前，我对 Medium 的入职流程做了两个微妙但强大的改变。令人惊讶的是，两个都不是工程特定的，也和代码走查或教程完全无关。我在这里和你分享它们，以及第三个快速和团队新成员建立对齐的额外技巧。

First Impression第一印象

The first day of a new job can be daunting, overwhelming, and anxiety inducing—so no matter how much other onboarding classes or codelabs or dev environment setup documents you have in place, one of the highest impact ways you can put someone at ease is the first impression they have when they show up for work. I set the first impression with a beautiful welcome letter on their desk. Every time a new engineer joined, I customized their welcome letter, printed it out on high-quality cardstock, and signed it with a pen, "Welcome! ~Medium Engineering." The letter expressed the team's enthusiasm at their joining, followed by a beautifully formatted schedule of their first day. I included the name of their onboarding buddy (see the next tip) as well as a pointer to a guide to set up their dev environments to work on in between meetings.

新工作的第一天可能令人畏惧、不知所措、焦虑——所以无论你有多少其他入职课程、codelab 或开发环境搭建文档，让某人放松的最高影响方式之一是他们来上班时的第一印象。我在他们桌上放一封漂亮的欢迎信来设定第一印象。每次新工程师加入，我定制他们的欢迎信，用高质量卡纸打印，用笔签名：「欢迎！~Medium 工程部」。信表达团队对他们加入的热情，接着是精美排版的第一天日程。我包括他们入职伙伴的名字（见下一个技巧）以及一个指向搭建开发环境指南的指针，让他们在会议之间做。

— 第 179 页 —

This practice was soon adopted by the rest of the company. In a day of overwhelming new accounts, new people, laptop setup, and calendar invites for onboarding events for the next week or so, a simple and personal reference to what they need to feel welcome and get through that first day is key.

这个做法很快被公司其他人采用。在充满新账户、新人、笔记本设置、未来一周左右入职活动日历邀请的一天里，一个简单个人的关于他们需要什么感到受欢迎和度过第一天的参考是关键。

Onboarding Buddy入职伙伴

The biggest inconsistency I found across different engineers' onboarding experiences was whether they had adequate access to someone to whom they could ask any question. The most impactful change I made to the onboarding process was to assign every new hire an onboarding buddy, who they were seated next to (if not remote). After they agreed to be a buddy, I'd send them an email detailing their responsibilities. Their highest priority for the first two to three weeks was to be available to the new hire to answer questions, pair-program, direct them to the appropriate people, and so on. I also required that on the new hire's first day, the buddy have a conversation with the new engineer, making that priority explicit. "My highest priority is getting you up to speed, so even if I look busy, feel free to ask me questions any time. Even if I don't know the answer, I can point you to the right person."

我发现不同工程师入职体验之间最大的不一致是他们是否能充分接触到一个可以问任何问题的人。我对入职流程做的最有影响的改变是给每个新员工分配一个入职伙伴，坐在他们旁边（如果不是远程）。在他们同意做伙伴后，我会发邮件详细说明他们的责任。他们前两到三周的最高优先级是对新员工有空回答问题、结对编程、指引他们找合适的人等。我还要求在新员工第一天，伙伴和新工程师对话，明确那个优先级。「我最高优先级是让你上手，所以即使我看起来忙，随时问我问题。即使我不知道答案，我也能指给你对的人。」

The onboarding buddy significantly reduced the barrier to asking for help. Getting someone set up and up to speed in days instead of weeks helps put them on a trajectory to be successful for their time at the company.

入职伙伴显著降低了求助门槛。在几天而不是几周内让某人搭好上手，帮他们走上在公司期间成功的轨道。

Powerful Questions to Build Alignment建立对齐的有力问题

As companies grow, they begin to codify their onboarding processes to scale with the scaling engineering team. But there is no one-size-fits-all; one engineer might thrive under light supervision, whereas another needs more guidance and guardrails. What became clear to me is that in all the conversations about building onboarding processes, there was very little about how differently individuals learn—how some like to be thrown into the deep end with a meaty project, and some like to have their hands held for a few days before leaving the nest. Ask a few of these powerful questions early on, and the answers might surprise you:

随着公司成长，他们开始把入职流程成文化以随工程团队扩展。但没有一刀切；一个工程师在轻监督下可能茁壮成长，而另一个需要更多指导和护栏。我清楚的是，在所有关于建设入职流程的对话中，很少关于个人学习方式多么不同——有人喜欢被扔进深水区做一个有分量的项目，有人喜欢离开巢前被牵几天手。早期问几个这些有力问题，答案可能让你惊讶：

— 第 180 页 —
  • What would be your ideal onboarding experience?你理想的入职体验是什么？
  • What's a time when you felt really excited and motivated on a new project and team? What about it was most motivating?有没有什么时候你在新项目和团队上感到非常兴奋和有动力？那里面什么最激励你？
  • What does being supported at work look like for you?工作中被支持对你来说是什么样？

Of course, as your team scales, you'll also add more standard onboarding resources. Those things are all important, but they also take a lot more time. These three tips I shared here—creating an inviting first impression, setting up an onboarding buddy system, and having an upfront conversation to discover what successful onboarding looks like for each new hire—don't require much time to implement, are extremely high leverage, and can really effectively smooth out some of the bumps as your team grows.

当然，随着团队扩展，你也会加更多标准入职资源。那些都重要，但也花更多时间。我这里分享的三个技巧——创造吸引人的第一印象、建立入职伙伴系统、提前对话发现对每个新员工成功的入职是什么样——不需要很多时间实施，是极高杠杆的，能非常有效地在团队成长时抚平一些颠簸。
